title: Causal role of human hippocampus in relational structure learning and inference
title_zh: 人类海马体在关系结构学习和推理中的因果作用
abstract: Abstract When meeting new individuals or known individuals in new circumstances, we intuitively map out their relationships—not merely through direct experience, but by inferring new connections on the basis of prior relational knowledge. How such relational knowledge is represented and used in the brain remains a long-standing question in cognitive neuroscience. Here, using a behavioural task and computational modelling, we show that participants ( N = 36) leveraged existing knowledge of relational structures to infer new relationships, facilitating adaptation in changing environments. Whole-brain neuroimaging identified consistent representations of relational structure in the hippocampus. To investigate the causal link between hippocampal representations and inference, we used neural network simulations to predict the behavioural effects of disrupting such representations. Consistent with this prediction, transcranial ultrasound stimulation of the human hippocampus ( N = 20), transiently modulating its activity, disrupted structure-based inference ( P < 0.001, Cohen’s d = −0.89, 95% confidence interval −1.41 to −0.36), providing empirical evidence for a causal role of hippocampus in relational-structure learning and structure-based inference.
abstract_zh: 摘要 当遇到新的个体或在新环境中遇到已知个体时，我们会直观地绘制他们的关系——而不仅仅通过直接经验，而是基于先前的关系知识推断新的连接。这种关系知识在大脑中如何表征和使用，一直是认知神经科学的长期悬而未决的问题。在此，利用行为任务和计算模型，我们表明参与者（N = 36）利用现有的关系结构知识来推断新的关系，从而促进在变化环境中的适应。全脑神经影像学检测到海马体中关系结构的一致表征。为了研究海马体表征与推理之间的因果联系，我们利用神经网络模拟来预测干扰此类表征的行为效应。与这一预测一致，经颅超声刺激人类海马体（N = 20），暂时调节其活动，干扰了基于结构的推理（P < 0.001，Cohen's d = -0.89，95%置信区间 -1.41 至 -0.36），为海马体在关系结构学习和基于结构的推理中起因果作用提供了经验证据。
